Every call requires a live SOV grant for its exact capability and scope; every mutating host operation stays declared but unreachable; the boundary reported is the process execution host and not an assumed machine; the host name is not exposed.
observed.observer_independence_basis: This session did not build services/host or adapters/host and did not edit either. The probe imports neither soveraeign_host_service nor local_host_adapter; it reaches the vertical only as a subprocess through scripts/sov_interface.py and the Console Service CLI. The participant's own suite at services/host/tests/test_host_service.py was not re-run as evidence: it imports the implementation directly and uses a fake adapter in nine of its eleven tests, so running it would have been the build checking itself.

projection_agrees_under_both_bindings.detail: show host.read-health renders JSON under MODEL and a text rendering under HUMAN, and both carry operation digest 031838d422336d53960865013df469593d861764f0945b69fe9229906172c080. The projection itself reports observed=no with an empty observation_ids, so the Node Interface agrees that nothing had observed this operation before this receipt.

no_grant_is_refused.detail: invoke host.read-health with no grant recorded anywhere returns reason_code AUTHORITY_REFUSED, failure_class GOVERNED_REFUSAL, at stage check-authority, and the refusal is appended to the journal as a RECEIPT entry rather than discarded.

no_scope_slips_through.detail: A foreign scope (host:someone-elses-machine), a wildcard scope (*), and an empty scope all return AUTHORITY_REFUSED. Read narrowly: with no live grant reachable, a correct scope would refuse too, so this shows no scope slips through, not that scope was the reason.

mutating_operations_unreachable.detail: All seven of host.restart, host.power-off, host.suspend, host.request-restart, host.apply-driver-update, host.install-utility and host.remove-utility return OPERATION_NOT_REACHABLE. None committed. The refusal fires before an envelope is built, not after an authority check.

host_name_not_disclosed.detail: Every byte printed by show, prove, and a refused invoke was scanned for this machine's platform.node() value, its USERNAME, and its USERPROFILE path. No surface disclosed any of the three.

prove_reaches_the_vertical_with_a_substi.detail: sov_interface.py prove drives host.read-health under both bindings to terminal outcome COMMITTED with standing_effect NONE, boundary PROCESS_EXECUTION_HOST, and same_host_semantics true. It uses adapter urn:soveraeign:adapter:node-interface-proof-host:v1, not adapters/host/local_host_adapter.py, so it proves the service, gateway and binding path and not the adapter that touches the host. The proof declares its own standing as BUILT_EVIDENCE_SETTLES_NOTHING.

success_path_reachable_through_declared_.detail: The Console Service CLI is the only declared surface that records a live grant, and it records one successfully (exit 0) at every state-root placement its declared arguments allow. Its journal always lands at <console_root>/journal/record-service.sqlite3, while scripts/sovnode/composition.py reads authority from RecordService(<state_root>/record). Three placements were tried - console root equal to the state root, to <state_root>/console, and to <state_root>/record - and all three left invoke at AUTHORITY_REFUSED. No combination of declared arguments puts a Console-issued grant in the store the Node Interface reads.
success_path_reachable_through_declared_.consequence: The success path of the Host Service's only BUILT operation cannot be reached by any participant that refuses to import the implementation. The health snapshot, its schema conformance, its limitation reporting, and the adapter diagnostic non-leakage defended by commits 33c7b98 and bbad5a6 are therefore unobserved here and cannot be observed by this path.
success_path_reachable_through_declared_.what_would_be_needed: A declared operation that records a grant into the state root the Node Interface reads - either a grant subcommand on scripts/sov_interface.py, or a --journal argument on the Console CLI, or a documented state-root layout that composes the two. Any of the three would make read-health independently witnessable.

refusal_is_visible_in_the_exit_status.detail: Both AUTHORITY_REFUSED on host.read-health and OPERATION_NOT_REACHABLE on host.power-off return process exit 0 from scripts/sov_interface.py. The Record Service CLI answers the same class of refusal with exit 2. A caller that reads exit status rather than parsing stdout cannot tell a governed refusal from a committed call on this surface.

correction_to_the_premise.claim_examined: that the Host Service crosses a process boundary
correction_to_the_premise.finding: It does not. A grep for subprocess, os.system, popen, Popen, os.exec and shell=True across services/host/ and adapters/host/ returns zero matches. The adapter's whole host reading is three pathlib read_text calls against /proc/meminfo, /proc/uptime and /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, plus os.getloadavg, os.cpu_count and three platform calls, all in-process. services/host/contracts/service.json forbids arbitrary-shell-or-command-execution and the code matches the manifest. On this Windows host the three /proc reads and os.getloadavg fail, so the real adapter would return nulls with six declared limitations.
correction_to_the_premise.why_it_matters_here: The lane prioritised this subject as boundary-crossing. It is not, which lowers its consequence relative to the journal, and it means no external-world effect was ever at stake in this observation.
